title: WPMS/2702/2014 of Smt Shalini @ Shalu Vs Manoj Kumar Chugh

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No.2702 of 2014
Smt. Shalini @ Shalu ÖÖ.Petitioner
 Versus
Manoj Kumar Chugh ÖÖÖ.Respondent
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J (Oral)
1. Mr. J.S. Virk, Advocate, holding brief of Mr.
Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
2. The present matter arises out of matrimonial
dispute. A suit for dissolution of marriage was filed by the
husband/respondent under Section 13 of the Hindu
Marriage Act which is pending in the Court of Family
Judge, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar being Suit
No.381 of 2009. The wife (present petitioner), in turn, has
filed an application for maintenance under Section 125
Cr.P.C. at Family Court, Bareilly, U.P. Meanwhile the
petitioner moved an application for reconciliation which
was rejected by the Family Court, Rudrapur.
3. Aggrieved, the petitioner filed present writ
petition before this Court praying for following reliefs:-
(i) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature
of mandamus to directing the learned Family
Court Judge to refer the divorce petition
bearing no. 381 of 2009 ìManoj Chugh Vs.
Shaliniî to Alternative Dispute Resolution
(A.D.R.) Center, Rudrapur for conciliation.
(ii)issue any other suitable writ, order or
direction which this Honíble Court may deem
fit and proper in the circumstances of the
case.
(iii)award the cost of writ petition in favour of
the petitioner.î
4. The learned Single Judge of this Court, before
whom this matter came initially vide order dated
08.12.2014 had directed that attempt be made for
mediation between the parties. The order dated
08.12.2014 reads as under:-

2
ìPresent petition has arisen out of
matrimonial dispute being Suit No. 381 of 2009
pending in the court of Judge, Family Court,
Rudrapur, Udham Singh Nagar. Learned counsel
for the petitioner has vehemently argued that
every possibility should be explored for amicable
settlement between the parties to save the
marriage and matter may be referred to
Mediation Centre of this Court.
 I find force in the submission made by
learned counsel for the petitioner.
 Let notice be issued to respondent fixing
08.01.2015 to appear before Mediation Centre of
this Court to explore the possibility of mutual
settlement between the parties. Petitioner shall
also remain present before the Mediation Centre
of this Court on the date fixed.
 Learned Mediator shall explore every
possibility for mutual settlement between the
parties and he shall be at liberty to take, as
many future sittings, as he may deem fit.
 Till report of the Mediator comes, further
proceedings of Suit No.381 of 2009 shall remain
stay.
CLMA No. 13971 of 2014 stands disposed
of accordingly.î
5. Thereafter, the matter was sent for mediation by
the trained mediators by the Court and in the mediation
proceedings, the parties agreed as follows:-
 1. That both the parties shall stay together at
Haridwar as husband and wife along with their
children who were born out of this wedlock
namely Km. Maanya on 20.06.1996 & Master
Shahil on 13.04.2001.
 2. That petition No. 381 of 2009 U/S 13 (1) 1(a) &
1 (b) of Hindu Marriage Act read with Section 7
(d) of Family Court Act pending before Family
Judge, Rudrapur Distt. Udham Singh Nagar,
shall be withdrawn by Mr. Manoj Kumar Chugh.
 3. That the proceedings Under Sec. 125 (3) of
Cr.P.C. initiated by Smt. Shalini @ Shalu
pending before Family Court at Bareilly (U.P.)
shall be withdrawn by Smt. Shalini @ Shalu.
 4. That Mr. Manoj Kumar Chugh shall make all
endeavour to ensure that his daughter Maanya
and Son Shahil are admitted in school/college
for the further education at Haridwar in the
next ensuing academic session.

3
 5. That parties deeply regret for their long five year
separation from each other and pray to God that
the same is not repeated in future.
 6. Both the parties have settled their disputes out
of their own free will, without any fear, force,
coercion or undue influence from any side.î

6. Such proceedings are placed before this Court
bearing wherein the signatures of the petitioner as well as
respondent. Both the petitioner (wife) as well as
respondent (husband) are present before this Court and
affirmed clearly that such a settlement has been made by
them on 22.01.2015.
7. In view thereof, since the wife (petitioner) had
already given an undertaking of settlement that she will
withdraw all the cases filed against the respondent
(husband), nothing further needs to be said. As regards
the case filed by the respondent (husband) against the
petitioner (wife) which is regarding Section 13 of Hindu
Marriage Act, let the order be passed by the Family Judge,
Rudrapur, Udham Singh Nagar in the light of the order
passed by this Court.
8. In view of the above observation and direction,
the writ petition stands disposed. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 23.01.2015
ML
